correctness.rationale: Positive diagonal scaling reduces every \(2\times2\) Stieltjes matrix to one coupling parameter without changing signs. Direct SOR multiplication gives the exact second-iterate response, whose only potentially negative coefficient is proportional to \(3-2\omega+\omega^2\rho^2\). Complete quadratic analysis yields the fixed-coupling frontier and the robust limit \(\omega=3/2\). The first-iterate and one-dimensional minimality claims are separately proved, and the embedded exact-rational replay verifies the algebraic formulas and witness.

originality.rationale: Classical convergence, spectral-radius, Stieltjes-matrix, and weak-splitting results are treated as prior work. The accepted statement is the exact finite-horizon second-iterate positivity phase diagram and its robust \(3/2\) frontier. Targeted semantic and bibliographic searches found no implication-equivalent statement, and the most relevant accessible full texts do not analyze coordinatewise signs of the second iterate. The unavailable full text of the closest weak-regularity note remains an explicit risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Yun's 2005 weak-regularity note was not recovered, so an equivalent finite-iterate observation there cannot be excluded.
Classical SOR monographs and older literature on monotone matrix iterations may contain the two-dimensional second-iterate formula under different terminology.
The accepted result does not classify third and later iterates, so it should not be interpreted as an all-iteration positivity range.

value.rationale: Stieltjes systems have nonnegative inverses, so nonnegative forcing produces a nonnegative exact solution; a negative SOR coordinate is therefore a meaningful transient shape failure. The theorem resolves the earliest possible failure mechanism, gives a complete two-parameter phase diagram for the minimal dimension, and reveals a robust safety frontier \(\omega=3/2\) that is strictly larger than the matrix-splitting weak-regularity boundary. The exact positive witness makes the distinction operationally testable.
